pitch.q: A member walks by talking on their phone. What do you do?
pitch.a: Let them pass — never pitch someone on the phone
pitch.why: On the phone = off limits. Greet the next member.

pitch.q: A member says "No thanks." What do you do?
pitch.a: Smile, thank them, let them go
pitch.why: One no and go. Every time.

pitch.q: A member waves you off without saying a word.
pitch.a: Treat it as a no — let them go
pitch.why: A wave-off is a no. One no and go.

pitch.q: A member ignores your greeting and keeps walking.
pitch.a: Let them go, greet the next member
pitch.why: Never chase or crowd.

pitch.q: A member said no earlier, then walks back up with a question.
pitch.a: Help them — they came to you
wrong: Send them to an AT&T store
pitch.why: One no and go means you don’t chase. If they come back, help them.

pitch.q: How many times can you pitch a member who said no?
pitch.a: Zero — one no and go
pitch.why: A second ask after a no is a compliance issue.

pitch.q: Where do you engage members from?
pitch.a: At the kiosk — never follow them through the warehouse
pitch.why: Stand where the traffic is, but stay at your kiosk.

pitch.q: Customer asks "So it’s free?"
pitch.a: Never say free — give the monthly price and the term
pitch.why: "Free" without the term attached leads to cancellations.

pitch.q: You want to close faster by saying "this ends today." It doesn’t.
pitch.a: Never invent urgency
pitch.why: A fake deadline is the fastest way to a cancellation.

pitch.q: Who signs the tablet?
pitch.a: The customer, themselves, in person
pitch.why: Never touch the customer’s signature.

pitch.q: Customer asks something that isn’t on the sheet.
pitch.a: "Let me confirm that before I tell you wrong."
pitch.why: Quote only what’s written. Confirm everything else.

pitch.q: Which statement about the VIP line is compliant?
pitch.a: "You get a dedicated Costco VIP support line."
pitch.why: Promise the access, never the outcome.

pitch.q: Two reps are chatting with each other at the kiosk.
pitch.a: Break it up — a huddle looks like a closed kiosk
pitch.why: Two reps talking to each other is a closed kiosk.

pitch.q: A Costco employee asks you to stop doing something.
pitch.a: Comply politely, tell your manager the same day
pitch.why: Never argue with store staff. Escalate the same day.

pitch.q: A customer gets angry and starts arguing.
pitch.a: Stay calm, don’t argue, offer the VIP line or your manager
pitch.why: Never argue or talk back.

pitch.q: Can you quote an offer from memory?
pitch.a: No — from the current sheet or system
pitch.why: Offers change on the client’s cycle, not yours.

pitch.q: A household of 2 — you could add 3 extra lines to hit numbers.
pitch.a: Don’t oversell — sell what fits the household
pitch.why: Add-ons that don’t fit come back as chargebacks with your name on them.

pitch.q: Can you promise the trade-in credit comes off today?
pitch.a: No — credits are monthly and start within 3 cycles
pitch.why: Credits are applied monthly, not off the price on day one.

pitch.q: You see a coworker keep pitching a member who said no.
pitch.a: Step in politely and tell your manager
wrong: Post it in the group chat
pitch.why: Compliance beats production. Always.

pitch.q: What’s the goal of the first 5 seconds?
pitch.a: A friendly question they can answer easily
pitch.why: Ask before you tell.

pitch.q: Which opener is best?
pitch.a: "Hi! Quick question — who do you have for your phone right now?"
pitch.why: Short, friendly, and easy to answer.

pitch.q: Who should you greet?
pitch.a: Everyone who isn’t on the phone
pitch.why: Don’t prejudge. You can’t see a bill by looking at a jacket.

pitch.q: How do you get your opener to sound natural?
pitch.a: Say it out loud 20+ times before your shift
pitch.why: The opener has to bore you before it sounds natural to them.

pitch.q: What number do you need first?
pitch.a: Their total monthly bill, all in
pitch.why: The all-in bill decides whether there’s a conversation.

pitch.q: Customer says "I have an iPhone 15." What’s your next question?
pitch.a: "Are you thinking about the new 18 Pro?"
pitch.why: An iPhone 15 in any condition gets top tier toward the 18 Pro.

pitch.q: Customer wants the iPhone 18 Pro. Which plan do you recommend?
pitch.a: Premium 2.0, for the full $1,200
pitch.why: Show the side-by-side: $1,200 vs $930 vs $500. Then let them choose.

pitch.q: Which question sets up Next Up Anytime?
pitch.a: "How often do you like getting a new phone?"
pitch.why: "Every year" = Next Up customer.

pitch.q: Customer doesn’t want to trade their phone in. What’s your move?
pitch.a: Tiered Offer — ask if it’s a new line or an upgrade
pitch.why: e.g. 17 Pro: $9.99 new line / $14.99 upgrade.

pitch.q: What’s the structure of every rebuttal?
pitch.a: Acknowledge → answer → ask
pitch.why: Finish on a question so the conversation stays yours.

pitch.q: Why end a rebuttal with a question?
pitch.a: If you end on your answer, they use the silence to leave
pitch.why: A question keeps you steering.

pitch.q: "I’m happy with what I have."
pitch.a: "Totally fair. What are you paying now, all in?"
pitch.why: Acknowledge, then ask for the bill.

pitch.q: "I don’t have time right now."
pitch.a: "Give me your bill total and I’ll tell you in 30 seconds if it’s worth it."
pitch.why: Respect their time. Offer a 30-second check.

pitch.q: "I need to talk to my spouse."
pitch.a: "Makes sense. Let’s get the numbers on paper. Are they free by phone now?"
pitch.why: Treat it as a household decision and make it easy.

pitch.q: "I’m still paying off my phone."
pitch.a: "There’s a path for that. How much is left on it?"
pitch.why: Carrier Switcher can reimburse up to $800 per line (36-month commitment).

pitch.q: "I’ll just do it online."
pitch.a: "Online there’s no $100 shop card, no waived fee, no VIP line."
pitch.why: Name what they only get at the kiosk.

pitch.q: "I had a bad experience with AT&T."
pitch.a: "I believe you. Buying here gets you the Costco VIP line. Was it billing or the device?"
pitch.why: Acknowledge, show what’s different, then ask.

pitch.q: "Is this going to raise my bill later?"
pitch.a: Answer fully: first bills, credit timing, terms
pitch.why: This answer decides whether the sale sticks. Never soften it.

pitch.q: "$10 more a month for Next Up? No thanks."
pitch.a: "Fair if you keep phones a few years — skip it."
pitch.why: Never force it and never call it free.

pitch.q: "My phone is cracked, it’s worth nothing."
pitch.a: "If it’s an iPhone 14–17, cracked still gets top tier."
pitch.why: Any condition, except the 16e.

pitch.q: "Why should I get Premium? It costs more."
pitch.a: "On the 18 Pro, Premium is the only way to the full $1,200."
pitch.why: Show the gap: $270 over Extra, $700 over Value.

pitch.q: "Is the shop card real?"
pitch.a: "Yes. It’s texted within 20 business days and never expires."
pitch.why: Digital card, no redemption steps.

pitch.q: "I’ll think about it."
pitch.a: "Totally. What part do you want to think over — the price or the phone?"
pitch.why: Find the real objection. No fake urgency.

pitch.q: Best close for Next Up Anytime?
pitch.a: "Want me to add it so next year is a five-minute visit?"
pitch.why: Make the future visit easy.

pitch.q: Which is a stronger close?
pitch.a: "256 or 512 gigs?"
pitch.why: An easy choice moves the deal forward.

pitch.q: Before the customer leaves, what do you ALWAYS cover?
pitch.a: VIP line, first 3 bills, trade-in shipping steps
pitch.why: That’s what prevents cancellations and callbacks.

pitch.q: When does a sale actually count?
pitch.a: When it activates
pitch.why: A written sale isn’t a paid sale until it activates.

pitch.q: Trade-in deal. What must they hear before they sign?
pitch.a: 30 days to ship, and it can’t be returned
pitch.why: Say it every time, out loud.

pitch.q: You just got a rude no. What happens to your face?
pitch.a: Reset — the next member can read the last one on you
pitch.why: Don’t let a no change your face.

pitch.q: Last hour of the shift, it’s slow.
pitch.a: Keep greeting — that’s where reps quietly quit
pitch.why: Work the full shift.

pitch.q: Why log every conversation?
pitch.a: You can’t fix a number you don’t track
pitch.why: Notebook out, every shift.

pitch.q: End of shift — what’s your debrief?
pitch.a: 3 things I learned, 3 things I need help with
pitch.why: That’s how you get better daily.

pitch.q: Compliance vs. production — which wins?
pitch.a: Compliance, always
pitch.why: Somebody lost a store over every rule.

iPhone trade-in.b: iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max only. The base iPhone 17 is not eligible.

Premium legacy = Premium 2.0 column. UYW Starter / Starter SL / other legacy = $930 top, $350 basic.
Want the 18 Pro or Pro Max? Recommend Premium 2.0 — it’s the only plan that pays the full $1,200 ($270 more than Extra, $700 more than Value).

$1,150 with any Pixel or $35+ on Premium, Extra and Legacy Starter. Value: $500.
On Android, Premium and Extra pay the same. Value is always $500.

No trade-in.h: First question: new line or upgrade?
No trade-in.b: Prices differ. iPhone 17 Pro 256GB: $9.99 new line / $14.99 upgrade. iPhone 17 Pro Max 256GB: $14.99 new line / $19.99 upgrade.
Pixel 10a $5.99 · Pixel 11 $10.99 · Motorola Edge $8.99 · razr+ (2026) $12.99. The moto g (2026) is not sold at Costco.
Credits over 36 months, starting within 3 cycles. Tax on full retail at sale. If Next Up Anytime is added, the $10/mo still applies.

Deal rules.b: Ship the trade-in within 30 days of activation. Credits start within 3 bill cycles.
The line isn’t in good standing, or another line on the account is cancelled within 90 days.
Turn off Find My / activation lock, factory reset, remove the SIM (older devices), use AT&T’s kit, one device per box, photo the label.
Once shipped, it can’t be returned and data can’t be recovered. Check live value at tradein.att.com.

Bundle.b: Buy a Pixel 11, 11 Pro or 11 Pro XL on installment (any plan, new or upgrade) + the watch on installment on a new watch line, within 14 days of each other.

Costco perks.b: Per line, on an eligible device purchase. Texted within 20 business days. Never expires. Status: rewardcenter.att.com.
$35 activation/upgrade fee waived · AutoPay & Paperless $10/mo per line with ACH ($5 debit).
Carrier Switcher up to $800/line (stay 36 months). AT&T Appreciation up to 20% (att.com/appreciation within 30 days).

Next Up Anytime.b: $10/mo per line. Upgrade after 1 payment. AT&T’s best offers unlock at 33% paid.
Every upgrade through Costco AT&T: fee waived, another $100 shop card, $50 in credits ($5/mo × 10) per line.
Qualify ("How often do you like a new phone?") → Explain → Stack Costco → Close ("Want me to add it so next year is a five-minute visit?").

Member care.b: (833) 950-4601. Promise the access, never the outcome.
Bill 1: partial month + month in advance + fees. Bill 2 may still be higher. Bill 3: settled, with discounts back-dated to bill 1.
A tax hold per device as each ships. Temporary duplicates drop off.
att.com/checkmyorder (99- order # + ZIP) · att.com/getstarted · number transfer takes up to 1 hour.

Compliance.b: Never pitch a member who is on a phone call. Let them pass and greet the next person.
"No," a wave-off, or being ignored all count as a no. Smile, thank them, let them go. Never ask twice, never follow. If they come back to you, help them.
Engage from your kiosk. Never follow members through the warehouse or crowd them.
Never say "free." Never invent urgency. Quote only from the current sheet. "Let me confirm that before I tell you wrong."
The customer signs the tablet themselves, in person. Don’t oversell lines the household doesn’t need.
Never argue with a customer, store staff or a teammate. Comply, then tell your manager the same day.
Say "You get a dedicated Costco VIP support line." Never say "they’ll fix anything," "no hold times," or "they’ll credit you."

Opening.b: Open with an easy, friendly question, not a pitch: "Hi! Quick question — who do you have for your phone right now?"
Everyone who isn’t on the phone. Don’t prejudge — you can’t see a bill by looking at a jacket.
Say your opener out loud 20 times before your first shift, and 20 more on the drive in.

Discovery.b: Their total monthly bill, all in.
"Are you trading in a phone today?" Yes → trade-in grid. No → Tiered Offer (ask: new line or upgrade?).
Show Premium vs Extra vs Value side by side ($1,200 / $930 / $500) and recommend Premium.
"How often do you like getting a new phone?"

Rebuttals.b: Acknowledge → answer → ask. Finish on a question or they use the silence to leave.
"Totally fair — most people are until they see the breakdown. What are you paying now, all in?"
"I won’t hold you up. Give me your bill total and I’ll tell you in 30 seconds if it’s worth a conversation."
"Makes sense. Let’s get the exact numbers on paper so you’re not guessing tonight — are they free by phone now?"
"That’s the most common situation I see. There’s a reimbursement path — how much is left, roughly?"
"You can — but online there’s no $100 Costco shop card, no waived fee, and no VIP line. Two minutes here saves the callback."
"I believe you. Buying here gets you the Costco VIP line instead of the general queue. Was it billing or the device?"
Answer completely: first bills, when credits start, promo terms, agreement length. Never soften it.
"If it’s an iPhone 14–17, cracked still gets the top credit."
"Totally. What part do you want to think over — the price or the phone?"

Closing.b: "256 or 512?" beats "So what do you think?"
"Want me to add it so next year is a five-minute visit?"
VIP line (833) 950-4601 · bills 1–3 · trade-in: 30 days, Find My off, one device per box.
It activates. A written sale isn’t a paid sale.

Mindset.b: Always. Somebody lost a store over every rule.
The next member can read the last one on your face.
The last hour is where most reps quietly quit.
Log every conversation. End of shift: 3 things I learned, 3 things I need help with.
